evidence: Traupman 206: flūmen, amnis (with no distinction as to size)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: first a broad, swift-flowing water, so often a large river or a torrent in the poets.
A river in general; Traupman gives it for “tributary”, which it does not specially mean (fluviī in eum īnfluunt, rivers flow into it).

phrases.latin: «Tagus est,» inquit pater, «quī Lisbōnam praeterfluit et ibi in mare effunditur.»
phrases.english: “It’s the Tagus,” said Dad, “which flows past Lisbon and there pours into the sea.”
phrases.source: Libellus V, Lisbōna: castellum et ōceanārium

phrases.english: the Tiber rising in the Apennines
